newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker to manage UK chip plant logistics.
newsitem.headline: Schenker to manage UK chip plant logistics.

text.p: Schenker International AG said it has won a logistics contract for the new Siemens AG chip plant in Newcastle, England.
The worldwide freight forwarder will manage equipment logistics for the Siemens semi-conductor factory which is currently under construction there, a company statement said.
But it did not put a value on the contract or give a timescale for its duration.
The Newcastle plant will be the second Siemens chip plant in Europe after Dresden, where production started in November 1995.
Schenker was also responsible for organising the Dresden equipment logistics and transported some 2,000 tonnes of freight there from the U.S., Japan and Europe over 17 months, the statement added.

This included managing the entire logistics chain from supplier to customer and creating an information system to check real-time shipment status, Schenker Germany managing director Michael Korn said.
A Dresden-based Schenker project team oversaw air cargo transport to Frankfurt with Lufthansa Cargo AG or to Luxembourg and onward overland transport to Dresden.
Special packing prevented transport damage which could have ruined the equipment and cost Siemens millions of marks in lost production time, Schenker said.
The forwarder also carried out export handling at Tokyo-Narita and Dallas/Fort Worth airports through local offices.
Schenker's SWORD communications and information system was used to link suppliers, clients and customs for tracing and tracing needs.

Schenker International is part of the Schenker-Rhenus AG transport group, a subsidiary of trading conglomerate Stinnes AG which, in turn, is owned by Veba AG. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
